A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable text, figures, tables, and equations. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A–E. The retained content and relocated personality-generator experiment can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original code-generation experiments across seven LLMs and four datasets, including prompting and personality-generation comparisons in Tables 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds personality-model comparisons, ablations, multiple-candidate results, and resource measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Figure 1 retain the same pipeline: GPT-4o generates a task-specific MBTI type and description, which condition code generation. The added Big Five, generic-description, and S/N-only variants are experimental comparisons or ablations; the proposed procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Python code-generation coverage: MBPP Sanitized, MBPP+, HumanEval+, and APPS. The added experiments use the existing MBPP Sanitized benchmark without introducing a new task, domain, or population.

E2.justification: v2 adds Big Five prompting across seven LLMs, a generic MBTI-description template for Qwen-Long, and an S/N-only control. These extend the existing personality-prompting comparisons. Earlier comparators remain, including the personality-generator comparison relocated to Appendix B.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds evaluation with five and ten generated candidates per task and pass@5/pass@10 metrics on MBPP Sanitized. This experiment includes five LLMs, excluding Qwen-Long and DeepSeek-Coder V2 because of stated API constraints. Main benchmark sampling and model configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the analyses: INTJ/ISTJ task overlap in Figure 3, generic versus task-specific descriptions in Section 5.4, MBTI versus Big Five in Section 5.5, and S/N-only versus full MBTI in Appendix C. The earlier personality-generator analysis is retained in Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs per LLM–dataset combination and report average pass rates. v2 adds a citation about nondeterminism but no new seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Multiple-candidate evaluation does not establish increased repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: All percentage entries in retained Tables 2–5 and v1 Table 6/v2 Table 7 match. Substantial new results cover personality comparisons, task overlap, ablations, pass@5/pass@10, and costs. For example, the generic-description control scores 65.5% versus 80.8% for task-specific descriptions on Qwen-Long; newly reported GPT-4o pass@10 is 82.0% for Direct and 93.9% for Personality.

T1.justification: The original pass-rate formulation is unchanged. Appendix D supplies the standard pass@k formula for the added evaluation, without substantive new mathematical reasoning. The added cognitive-style rationale is conceptual; neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: personality guidance improves 23 of 28 LLM–dataset combinations, reaches a maximum 12.9-point gain, and combines with other prompting strategies. Added experiments support these claims without redefining their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about complementary INTJ/ISTJ strengths, why MBTI cognitive preferences suit coding better than Big Five, and potential benefits from mimicking human cognitive processes. Section 8 also newly acknowledges missing ground-truth personality labels and the resulting inability to directly assess assignment accuracy or determine the performance upper bound.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data release statement and repository address, a full personality example and prompting templates in Appendix A, and token consumption, API prices, GPU runtimes, and four-A800 deployment information in Appendix E. These substantially expand documented reproducibility information; repository availability itself was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting Big Five modeling, pass@k evaluation, prompting, and nondeterminism, including John et al., Chen et al. on CodeT, Huang et al. on EffiLearner, and Ouyang et al. The principal research positioning remains unchanged; publication and author-format updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: Most original prose and section ordering are retained. The main reorganization moves the former RQ5 to Appendix B, introduces personality modeling as RQ5, and adds Discussion, acknowledgments, and appendices. Local wording, author-header, and bibliographic edits accompany these additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds the overlap diagram, personality example, and prompting panels in Figures 3–5, plus Tables 6 and 8–10. It also resizes the workflow figure and relocates the earlier generator-comparison table into Appendix B as Table 7. These substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The new framework, description, and dimension controls provide useful additional support, while pass@k results, prompt examples, resource reporting, and declared code/data access improve evaluation and reproducibility. The gains are limited by concentration on MBPP Sanitized, and the new cognitive-mechanism explanations exceed what the experiments directly establish. Overall, the unchanged core study is better supported and documented.
